record.paper_title: Open problems posed at the tenth International conference on fuzzy set theory and applications (FSTA 2010, Liptovsky Jan, Slovakia)
record.original_question: In a sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebra, every nonzero element x has a unique basic decomposition x = w_x plus the orthogonal sum of kappa-indexed atom multiples k_kappa a_kappa, where w_x is sharp, the a_kappa are atoms, and each k_kappa is a positive integer not equal to the order of a_kappa. Does every sharply dominating homogeneous Archimedean atomic effect algebra admit an analogous decomposition property of its elements by atoms of the algebra?

artifact.status_search_result: Search results show extensive work on the basic decomposition property (BDE) in sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras (Riečanová, Niederle, and others), including results on inheritance of BDE in sublattices and atomic blocks. No source located explicitly resolves the decomposition question for the broader class of sharply dominating homogeneous Archimedean atomic effect algebras without the lattice assumption, so the current status appears unverified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: More about sharp and meager elements in Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sharp/meager elements and basic decomposition in sharply dominating Archimedean atomic lattice effect algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on BDE in the lattice case; broader homogeneous case not explicitly resolved here.
